purpose: Compact functional-chain and gateway scaffold for the World Map. Chains describe connected capabilities and dependencies; they are not political blocs and are not ordinary top-bar controls.

arctic.label: Arctic
arctic.description: Eight Arctic states connected through geography, security, shipping, science, communications and resource/infrastructure questions.
arctic.source_note: Arctic Council state membership provides the empirical state spine; project North interpretation remains separate.

north-atlantic.label: North Atlantic
north-atlantic.description: Overlapping sea, cable, aviation, energy, security and trade relationships across the North Atlantic.
north-atlantic.source_note: Derived from the canonical European Coupling Programme and North Atlantic infrastructure logic.

baltic.label: Baltic
baltic.description: Baltic and adjacent states connected through grids, logistics, industry, defence and communications.
baltic.source_note: Derived from the canonical European Coupling Programme functional-chain definition.

northern-energy.label: Northern Energy
northern-energy.description: North Sea and Nordic energy resources converted through grids, interconnectors, storage and demand into wider European capability.
northern-energy.source_note: Canonical North capability-chain and European energy-network work.

european-industrial.label: European Industrial
european-industrial.description: Industrial capability created by coupled energy, capital, research, suppliers, transport, procurement and customer markets across Europe.
european-industrial.source_note: Canonical European Coupling Programme and Sector Atlas relationship-first model.

eastern-security.label: Eastern Security
eastern-security.description: Northern, Baltic and continental European capability connected to Ukraine through defence, logistics, finance, reconstruction and industrial learning.
eastern-security.source_note: Canonical European Coupling Programme functional-chain definition.

european-strategic-autonomy.label: European Strategic Autonomy
european-strategic-autonomy.description: A capability chain concerned with reducing fragile single-point dependencies while preserving open, reciprocal external relationships.
european-strategic-autonomy.source_note: Canonical European Coupling Programme; not a claim of complete autonomy or a formal institution.

eurasian-interface.label: Eurasian / SCO-BRICS Interface
eurasian-interface.description: A multipolar Eurasian interface centered on overlapping SCO membership and wider BRICS/Eurasian relations; it does not imply a unified ideology or command structure.
eurasian-interface.source_note: SCO membership is empirical; wider East/BRICS interpretation is project-interpretive and must remain separate.

blue-pacific.label: Blue Pacific
blue-pacific.description: Pacific sovereign states connected by ocean geography, fisheries, climate resilience, security, communications and regional institutions.
blue-pacific.source_note: Pacific Islands Forum provides the empirical institutional spine; South-axis interpretation remains project-specific.

southern-african.label: Southern African
southern-african.description: SADC-region countries connected through trade, infrastructure, energy, mining, water, industrialisation and regional development systems.
southern-african.source_note: SADC membership is empirical; South-axis placement is separately versioned project interpretation.

gateway_model.rule: A gateway is an empirical system interface or chokepoint. Any comparison to the project's symbolic Door belongs only in deeper project metadata and never substitutes for infrastructure evidence.
